description: Card P's targets for "Diesel 2.0 L common rail": the invariants are hard; the rest are reported, never failed: their misses are the simulator's to-do list. Predicted strongest lines (not measured: the validation format has no line measure yet): the firing frequency, rpm/60 x 4/2, 26.7 Hz at the 800 rpm idle and 160 Hz at the 4800 rpm limiter.

targets.name: Invariant: starts warm and runs
targets.source: a warm engine started on its key runs and keeps running (engine.state 2)

targets.name: Invariant: within full scale
targets.source: 02-contracts.md, section 1: what process writes is within +-1

targets.name: Invariant: holds its limiter
targets.source: a rev limiter holds the speed within a few percent of where it cuts (some 100 to 200 rpm at 6500)

targets.name: Invariant: pulls away
targets.source: started, in gear and on the pedal, the car moves (a 36 t tractor at least 3 m/s in ten seconds)

targets.name: Invariant: stops at the key
targets.source: the key off stops the engine (engine.state 0 by the run's end)

targets.name: Starts cold
targets.source: a sound engine starts from the air's temperature within some four seconds of cranking and keeps running (a rule of thumb; makers' cold-start specifications are 2 to 5 s)

targets.name: Peak power
targets.source: published figures of its kind (makers' figures, firm): 1968 cc; 51 to 66 kW a litre

targets.name: Speed at peak power
targets.source: published figures of its kind (makers' figures, firm): 1968 cc: 3500 to 4200 rpm

targets.name: Peak torque
targets.source: published figures of its kind (makers' figures, firm): 1968 cc; BMEP 20.4 to 24.3 bar (a naturally aspirated petrol engine 10 to 13 bar, turbocharged 18 to 25, a modern truck diesel 20 to 25: Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 2)

targets.name: Speed at peak torque
targets.source: published figures of its kind (makers' figures, firm): 1968 cc: 1700 to 3000 rpm (a turbocharged engine's plateau: its whole span)

targets.name: Warm idle
targets.source: makers' service specifications of the kind: 750 to 900 rpm warm in neutral (a rule of thumb, firm to 100 rpm); the ECU is asked for 800

targets.name: Idle steadiness
targets.source: a warm idle's speed wanders some 20 to 50 rpm (a rule of thumb); a lope of more than 150 rpm over the range's top is a fault

targets.name: Boost at its target
targets.source: the build's own target (1.40 bar); a wastegate or vane loop holds a steady full load within some 0.1 bar of its target once spooled (makers' boost-control tolerances; judgement)

targets.name: Charge temperature under boost
targets.source: an air-to-air intercooler of 0.6 to 0.8 effectiveness leaves the charge some 10 to 50 K over the outside air at full boost (makers' and tuners' intake-air-temperature logs; judgement): reported so the over-delivery at a given boost can be judged (the lead's ask)

targets.name: Lambda at full load under boost
targets.source: a turbo diesel at full load runs lambda 1.2 to 2 (smoke-limited; Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 10)

targets.name: Port gas at full load
targets.source: the gas at a diesel's exhaust valve at full load, before the port and pipe cool it: some 850 to 1100 K (judgement: the header's 700 to 950 K, below, plus the port's cooling; Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 14)

targets.name: Header gas at full load
targets.source: a thermocouple a little way down a diesel's manifold reads some 700 to 950 K at full load (makers' pre-turbine limits near 1000 K; Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 14)

targets.name: Quarter mile: time
targets.source: Hale's rule, ET = 5.825 (lb/hp)^(1/3) s, with the kind's published power (115 kW) and the build's mass: 16.18 s; 5 % quicker to 15 % slower for the build's own tyres and launch (card I's test holds drag radials to 8 %)

targets.name: Quarter mile: trap speed
targets.source: Hale's rule, trap = 234 (hp/lb)^(1/3) mph: 37.7 m/s (136 km/h), within 8 % under to 6 % over

targets.name: Top speed
targets.source: where 0.85 of the kind's published power (115 kW) meets the build's drag area and 1.2 % rolling resistance at 1.225 kg/m^3: 216 km/h, within 7 % (a power balance, not a test)
